title: Futility look is one-sided: a skill trending to hurts stops at half the panel and is posted as not distinguished
resolution: Stop for futility only when conditional power is under 10% for a true effect of both plus and minus the planned MDD, so a skill whose interim estimate favors none runs the full panel and can read hurts. Print the interim estimate, its 95% interval and its direction at every stop, and have R48 treat an interim estimate in none's favor as a loss lead, not a plain null. Add both cases to O5's keyless dry run.

title: The 1.5x cost-per-solved guard can't be passed by most wave-1 told skills at the plan's own 2.2x to 5.0x multiples, and the plan doesn't say whether it binds
resolution: State whether the guard binds told skills and in which form (#169 binds it on H-inv as an upper bound <= 1.5, README.md:178). Print each skill's break-even gain beside its MDD in section 8 (at a 50% control rate: plan-eng-review +23, plan-devex-review and plan-design-review +30, devex-review +33, design-review +50, autoplan unreachable). Define solved for U's and X's cost figure, reuse #169's G3 definition in O4, and write the R48 rule that turns the ratio interval into KEEP or CUT-CANDIDATE. Ask Garry before admission whether 1.5x on hidden-test solves is the bar for a told skill.

title: The promise that wave 1 settles GST-1218 rests on an unnamed after pin and on a null inference the plan disowns
resolution: Replace 'A null rules out a gain of that size' with an interval rule: a gain is ruled out only above the upper 95% bound of told minus none, or against F2's break-even gain. Tie GST-1218's keep-or-cut reading to a told arm on the named after pin. If the pin isn't named by G admission, tell the Captain then that plan-eng-review's and plan-devex-review's rows can only inform GST-1218 (a forced-line verdict can't KEEP or CUT, line 27), and let the Captain choose between waiting and reading the forced line as information.

title: Central prices sit at half the house's real-task central (R3 amendment 4: 5x Verified) and the price-risk case stresses only the none session
resolution: Stress section 8 at the house central (5x Verified) and high (10x), with particle-1 at quick look 3's 0.41 of Opus, told multiples at 1.5x their central and the agent user at 2x, and print which rows survive and their MDDs. Show the wave-1 table's MDDs at both central and house central. Reuse R3 amendment 4's between-part projection check between admission, screening and confirmatory, so a stage that would push a skill's re-sized MDD past what can change its decision stops before it spends. Recheck particle-1's 2-point fit at admission's metered ratio before any particle-1 spend.

title: autoplan's told arm names no kind, voice count or gate setting; the before pin predates R66's kinds and the 5.0x price assumes the full panel
resolution: Freeze autoplan's told invocation in O1: the kind (crews now run --kind feature on features), the phases scope chooses, the outside voice and its model, the gate answer, and the exact slash line per pin. Meter that configuration on admission sessions before autoplan's place, size and MDD in the wave-1 table are fixed, align the four-way stand-in with it, and name the configuration in every autoplan verdict. If the after pin's default kind differs, the prereg says which one it tests and why.

title: Free within-family contrasts go unread: autoplan against plan-eng-review told and its stand-in on the 78 shared G tasks
resolution: Preregister as secondaries at no added spend: autoplan told minus plan-eng-review told and autoplan told minus plan-eng-review's stand-in on the 78 shared tasks, each with its cost-per-solved ratio, plus plan-devex-review told beside devex-review told on X's shared panel as a descriptive line. Draw autoplan's 78 tasks as a seeded subset of the 108 and run all G arms in the same interleaved batches.

title: U's wave-1 confirmatory buys a 15 to 16 point reading the plan says can't move a design skill to a cut
resolution: Apply section 8's rule for design-consultation and design-html to U's wave-1 rows: plan-design-review and design-review go to confirmatory only once a cheaper agent user passes the same calibration and the prereg's MDD is about 12 to 13. Otherwise they stop after admission with their price, exposure and calibration reading as FIX-METHOD, and most of their $3,299 plan stays unspent.

title: The branch design that cancels build noise is offered to design-review only; devex-review has the same after-build shape
resolution: Offer devex-review the same branch design: told continues from the none arm's own built tree with gstack installed before T2, so told pays only for T2 and build noise cancels. Admission measures its spread on the X slice and X's prereg uses it when its MDD comes out lower. State in section 4's arm table that T1 then runs without gstack installed.

title: Sections 1, 2, 5 and 9 still describe v1's arms and measures (stand-in and untold for every skill, autoplan in U and X, follow-up and judges in wave 1)
resolution: Edit section 1's question to none and told, with the stand-in where it runs; drop autoplan from section 2's U and X rows; in section 5's wave-1 table drop follow-up and judges and set autoplan's family to G; in section 9 mark the idea-only column as plan-eng-review only and drop the follow-up clause from plan-eng-review's saturation raise.

title: Lane amendments ask for ship and review spend the ceiling may not allow, and /review's K4 arms are priced both in the lane and as wave 2's $1,619 row
resolution: Make both lane amendments conditional on the Captain's decision on whether the $2,000 ceiling binds ship (the Captain's reading is that whole-gstack evals get the same, NOTES.md:1174). Price /review's K4 arms in one place only: either here as wave 2's row or in the lane's plan.

title: With Sol out of wave 1, a CUT-CANDIDATE would cut shipped skill text on Opus-only evidence
resolution: Label every wave-1 verdict as Opus 5.5 only and say in each CUT-CANDIDATE that Sol is untested. Consider a Sol admission-only row (12 x 2, none and told, about $55 to $75 a skill at R3a's Sol ratios) from each G and X skill's reserve, so a cut can say whether Sol's exposure or headroom differ.

title: One-tree screening on X's 0/0.5/1 and U's thirds scores makes the 40% in-band yield optimistic
resolution: Screen U and X on two none trees, or on a band the thin slice validates, and set their in-band yields from the slice's measured screen instead of 40%. Re-derive section 14's 190 and 240 valid-task needs, the mining reach and the authoring cost from that yield.

title: particle-1 rows print no tasks x trials or MDD
resolution: Print particle-1's size, MDD and expected none rate on the Opus-screened panel per skill in the wave-1 table, so its floor rule and the 2-point fit can be checked.

title: Wave 2 and 3 prices reuse wave-1 panels that are built only for admitted skills
resolution: Say that a reused-panel row is priced again without reuse if its family's wave-1 skills stop at admission, and show the five G-reuse rows (verify, deslop-shared-libs, context-save, context-restore, learn) at their stand-alone price.

title: This plan's own crew use sits outside the all-in skill ceilings
resolution: Charge this plan's crew use pro rata to the six wave-1 skills, or have the Captain record it in approvals/ as accepted program overhead, since the Captain's reading of the ceiling includes thread model use.

title: Agent user acts by role and accessible name at one 1280x720 viewport, so design-review's hierarchy, spacing, slop and mobile fixes and plan-design-review's responsive pass are invisible; the degraded fixture only tests a11y and function defects
resolution: Make the primary agent user vision-first (screenshot plus coordinate actions, no a11y text), keep a11y mode as a sensitivity, run one scenario per task at 375 wide, and add visual degraded fixtures with an identical a11y tree (demoted primary action, competing primaries, key control below the fold, mobile overflow) to admission row 4

title: Scenario completion is confounded with functional correctness; a design skill can win family U by making the feature work, and band screening on completion selects functionally hard tasks
resolution: Run a privileged reachability probe per scenario per tree; the design reading is completion on reachable scenarios, unconditional completion is a sensitivity; screen and admit on the conditioned reading and report 'helps by making it work' under its own name

title: Completion within a 25-step cap saturates for a frontier agent on any working UI; Krug claims effort and errors, which are only secondaries
resolution: Freeze a per-scenario step budget from gold's pilot median (about 1.5 times, at most 25); primary is completed within budget, raw completion secondary; admission reads gold versus degraded on that measure

title: U's hidden-test guard includes the PR's selector-bound e2e tests, so arms that redesign the screen fail them and design skills get marked as tradeoffs for doing their job
resolution: Guard on unit and integration tests only; print the PR e2e pass rate as a descriptive line outside the guard

title: No boot and seed contract for real web apps (database, migrations, seed, auth, stubbed services, offline); 'app does not start scores 0' mixes arm failures with rig failures and boot feasibility will cut U's yield
resolution: Freeze a per-task boot contract at authoring and state it to every arm; classify boot failures as arm (unsolved) or rig (gap); add an admission row that gold and base boot in at least 90% of runs and report boot yield per mined repo in the thin slice

title: Scenarios are unspecified as to state, so three happy paths would leave plan-design-review's empty, loading, error and edge states unmeasured
resolution: Freeze a scenario mix: where the feature has them, one scenario from the empty state and one requiring error recovery; tag scenarios by kind and print per-kind completion

title: U statements written from the PR and scenario goals that quote gold's labels leave design skills nothing to decide and hand the agent user gold's vocabulary
resolution: U statements give goal, data and constraints, never layout or labels; scenario goals use user language with no control names; the auditor checks both

title: The agent user is selected on the same thin-slice fixtures the admission instrument row reads, and both candidates are models under test
resolution: Select on half the fixtures and admit on the other half; add one cross-family candidate that is not a model under test

title: Judges compare screenshots whose states depend on each arm's agent-user path, with no order control or agreement statistic
resolution: Scripted capture of defined states (entry, empty, error, checker state via the reachability probe) at 375 and 1280 wide; both orders; print judge agreement; pin the rubric by sha256

title: Both design skills' mockup steps need the gstack designer, which calls OpenAI's image API with OPENAI_API_KEY; the no-other-key pin disables them silently and the '7 passes in order' detector does not record it
resolution: State that the designer is unavailable by construction in every U told cell, scope the claim to 'without generated mockups', and have the exposure detector record DESIGN_NOT_AVAILABLE; supplying a key needs its own route, price and OpenAI image terms check

title: R65 and custody: UI assets (fonts, icons, logos) carry licences and trademarks apart from the repo licence, and agent-user screenshots, aria snapshots, step logs and judge inputs reveal the repo and gold UI but are not in section 12's sealed list
resolution: Add an asset-licence check to V8, publish no task-app screenshot, seal agent-user and judge artifacts as panel material, and send judge calls with a data-collection deny

title: design-review's exposure detector names the Trunk Test from 1.93.34.0; the after pin may rename or restructure it
resolution: Freeze each design skill's exposure detector from the confirmatory pin's files, with keyless fixtures from that pin

title: Base-tree check cannot detect docs saturation: it tests whether the goal needs the feature, not whether it needs the docs; section 14's claim is wrong
resolution: Add a per-task docs-sensitivity fixture (gold artifact and gold --help, with the base tree's doc files) and an admission row: first success on gold docs at least 30 points above gold code with base docs, mirroring U's degraded-fixture drop; correct section 14

title: Goal 'use the new <feature> to <outcome>' names the feature that V4 already names in the statement, so the docs-only agent can find it in --help without the arm's docs
resolution: Write X goals in user words that state the outcome and withhold the feature's name; have the checker confirm the new surface ran (an exec-log shim or an outcome only that surface produces), and keep the base-tree check

title: CAP4:docs-only harness:channel interactive CLIs (TUIs, prompts, pagers; the probe's fzf --bind feature is one) can hang a no-terminal agent with no non-interactive rule or per-command timeout
resolution: Admit only goals completable non-interactively (or provide a scripted pty such as tmux with a documented driver), set a per-command timeout, set PAGER=cat and CI=1, and score a timed-out command as a failed command, never a gap

title: What counts as docs is defined three ways (section 3 list, section 10 'every doc file', arm-created files unaddressed), and 'no source tree' is unenforceable for Python and npm packages whose installed files are source
resolution: Freeze one doc-set rule per repo at authoring (globs from what the repo ships at base plus matching files the arm adds, plus --help and type files built from the arm's tree), and either declare installed package contents part of the published surface or restrict X to compiled CLIs in the pilot

title: Family X has no task file contract: goal file, checker interface and timing (after each turn or at the end), build recipe, offline dependency install, doc globs and artifact class are unnamed, so O3 and T-X will guess
resolution: Add X rows to the lane's task SPEC table (goal.md, docs-globs, build.sh with an offline mirror, check.sh with exit-code contract, run after every turn and read-only to the agent) before thin-slice authoring

title: CAP6:docs-only build:recovery an arm tree that fails to build or install the artifact, and a docs-only run lost to a provider error, have no rule separating arm failure (score 0) from rig gap, and no recovery
resolution: Score an arm-caused build or install failure as 0 with its cause printed; treat a measurement-agent upstream or rig failure as a gap rerun once with a named repair, counted under the 5% NO READ rule; give each a reason code in src/errors/codes.ts

title: X images carry no browser, but devex-review drives Aside or gstack's $B, asks for a docs URL in Step 0 and says to stop rather than substitute curl when no browser exists, so its told arm may stop before Step 1
resolution: Put Playwright and Chromium in X images for every arm as U does, and run a $0 probe of devex-review on a CLI fixture under the simulated user; read exposure from its gstack-review-log row (tthw_measured, dimensions_tested)

title: X yield is overstated: the DX tag (docs plus any index.ts, __init__.py, lib.rs or schema file) catches internal refactors and web-app APIs (memos leads), and X has no mining scope while U has 60 repositories
resolution: Tighten the tag to public-surface changes with a user doc change, list X's artifact classes (CLI binary, library package; servers deferred or given a boot contract), and set an X mining target sized to about 360 valid candidates

title: Admission row 4's docs-only bar has no unit and no per-task validity rule, so two broken goals can fail a whole family
resolution: Add V11: a task enters the pool only if gold reaches first success in at least 2 of 3 runs and base in 0 of 2; keep the family row as pooled over valid tasks

title: plan-devex-review asks for a mode under the simulated user: EXPANSION proposes scope beyond the statement, TRIAGE traces only install and hello world, and the '8 passes in order' detector ignores the mode
resolution: Freeze the mode the simulated user picks (POLISH for enhancement tasks) or record the mode and score exposure per mode's required passes

title: autoplan on family X counts as exposed when its own scope detector skips the DX phase, so autoplan (DX scope) can be scored without any DX review
resolution: For X rows, require the DX phase in autoplan's run.json as part of exposure, and report how often scope detection chose DX

title: X primary is confounded with build and correctness, and the hidden-test guard ('losing more than 10 points') has no statistic
resolution: Print the X primary on the subset where both arms' trees pass hidden tests as a sensitivity; define the guard as the 95% interval of told minus none on hidden tests lying wholly below minus 10 points

title: The plan names lanes/outcome-skills/ but no src/cli.ts row, subcommands, registry schema or reason codes, which AGENTS.md requires for every new command
resolution: State whether outcome-skills is a new cli row or subcommands of 'real', name each unit's entry command and its first smoke test, and list the reason codes O1 to O5 add

title: Wall time to first success mixes provider latency into a secondary
resolution: Report turns, tokens and failed commands to first success; keep wall time descriptive only

title: The fixed docs-only reader is Opus 5.5, the same family as the Opus row's writer, which may favour Opus-written docs over Sol and particle-1 docs
resolution: State the asymmetry in each X verdict, and in the pilot run a second reader family on a sample to size it

title: R65: docs may carry a licence apart from the code, and docs-only images bundle the artifact's dependency closure
resolution: Record a declared docs licence beside the SPDX id in V8, and state that task images stay private so dependency redistribution terms never apply

title: Per-skill plans assume both skills in a family pass admission; a lone survivor costs $1,986 to $2,376 at its planned size
resolution: Price the one-survivor branch per family in section 8. At planned sizes the survivor pays every unspent shared cost (bulk authoring, screening, the whole none arm, the prereg thread) and costs autoplan $1,986, plan-eng-review $2,272, plan-devex-review $2,357, devex-review $2,376, plan-design-review $2,319 and design-review $2,237. Freeze a re-size rule (drop the particle-1 row first, then trials, then tasks) and print the MDD it buys (about 15 to 17 in G and X, 18.6 to 19.2 in U), or stop the survivor when that MDD passes the bound in F4. Apply the same rule when one skill stops at the futility look.

title: Told prices come from sessions where the procedure mostly did not run, and the forced arm that decision 3 expects to run has no price
resolution: Add forced and told-exposed price rows to section 8. The only metered told session (R3a told /investigate, $0.424) had exposure 2 of 10, E0's $0.236 is a plain none session, and v2 deleted v1's forced row (told plus 15%, with panel v3's forced lines at 1.7 times told on plan units). Price the confirmatory on the arm that will run: forced at told x1.15 central and x1.5 as the risk case (planned designs $1,704 to $1,777 and $1,836 to $2,081, autoplan over its ceiling; re-sized G MDDs 14.4/15.0 and 16.2/15.6). Have admission meter exposed and unexposed told sessions separately, and freeze the pin at admission: a pin named after admission needs a new admission paid from the reserve.

title: Authoring is priced at TS's paid author and audit spend; the crew thread that mined, built, checked and sealed the tasks cost about five times that and has no line
resolution: Add a crew line per valid task for mining, building, checking and sealing, measured on each family's thin-slice thread and re-sized at admission. TS spent $7.93 of author and auditor calls plus $1.78 of VM for 7 valid tasks while its thread used about 43,500 credits before its /ship tail (GEVA-173.md:16), about $6.20 a valid task. Wave 1 needs about 800 valid tasks (G 372, U 192, X 237). At a fifth of TS's rate the planned designs cost $1,761 to $1,912 and re-size to MDDs of G 14.4/15.0, U 15.6 and X 14.4; at TS's full rate G alone needs about $2,300, more than both G reserves. Also price two preregs per family (admission and confirmatory) inside the $70 line, not one.

title: Admission has no MDD bound, so a skill whose metered prices buy a 19 to 20 point reading still spends its ceiling
resolution: Restore a power stop in admission criterion 5. Freeze per family the largest MDD worth buying (section 8 already treats 13 to 14 as able to settle keep-or-cut and about 20 as unable); a metered re-size above it stops the skill as FIX-METHOD (price) with its size and MDD printed, before bulk mining spends. Apply the same bound to the survivor re-size in F1.

title: Section 4 makes the task-clustered test primary and calls the repository reading the lane's sensitivity; the lane decides by repository, and the 1.2 factor sizes the repository test
resolution: Make the repository-clustered sign-flip the decision test in every family, as lanes/real-outcome/score/analysis.ts:183 does and section 10 already says for U and X, with the task-clustered reading as the sensitivity. Under repository clustering a task-level test keeps its power and loses its alpha (about 0.10 at the 1.44 variance inflation v2 assumes), so the 1.2 factor corrects the wrong test. Cap tasks per repository so each family has at least 20 repositories (src/runner/stats/gates.ts:177 makes fewer than 10 inconclusive), and add a repository random effect to the prereg's re-simulation, printing the MDD at ICC 0, 0.05 and 0.10, since 12 slice tasks can't estimate it.

title: The stated test matches neither existing scorer: gates.ts decides superiority one-sided with a min_effect, and the lane's look() has an efficacy interim, a 1.977 final boundary and an equivalence verdict
resolution: Name in section 4 the exact rule O4 runs: a two-sided sign-flip at 0.05 (0.025 under Holm) with min_effect 0, or gates.ts superiority one-sided at 0.025 per direction. Say that O4 does not reuse the lane's two-look O'Brien-Fleming look() (lanes/real-outcome/score/power.ts:11-12, analysis.ts:170-174) for the futility look and never emits same_within_margin, and re-simulate the MDD table at the boundary O4 actually uses.

title: Opus panels shrink to pay for particle-1 rows before particle-1's floor is read, so a floor drop leaves Opus underpowered for nothing
resolution: Read particle-1's floor on the admission slice (its admission is already paid) or on a first screened batch, and size the Opus panel after that read; if the floor fails, the particle-1 money returns to Opus's tasks before bulk screening closes. Today the rows cost autoplan 1.2 points (13.2 to 14.4) and X 1.2 and 0.6 (12.0/12.6 to 13.2/13.2), and the 0.08 price ratio comes from a review-only session where particle-1 took 11 turns to Opus's 4; at 0.3 the plan's G configuration moves plan-eng-review from 12.0 to 14.4, past the 2-point rule.

title: For plan-devex-review a told win cannot KEEP the skill text: told minus none carries the planning turn, and the de-confounding arm lost the budget to particle-1 rows
resolution: Say in section 8 that for plan-devex-review (and autoplan and plan-design-review) a helps reading means plan first and review helps, and goes to R48's idea-only path, not KEEP; GST-1218 can settle a cut on a null or a loss but not a keep on a win. State cost.py's joint selection rule (most added rows within 2 points). If the Captain wants the keep call settled, swap X's particle-1 rows for a bare plan-first arm on plan-devex-review (two turns, about 1.1 times none); the three-turn stand-in alone costs X 3.0 points (12.0 to 15.0) and fails the 2-point rule.

title: A null rules out a gain of that size is wrong: a non-significant estimate's 95% interval reaches about 1.4 times the MDD
resolution: With the MDD at 2.8 standard errors, an estimate up to 1.96 SE (0.7 MDD) is not significant and its upper bound reaches 3.9 SE (1.4 MDD, 18 to 22 points at v2's sizes); only an estimate near zero bounds gains near 0.7 MDD. Replace section 7's rules out only gains larger than the MDD and section 8's rules out a gain of that size with: a null rules out gains above its interval's upper bound, which the results post prints per skill, and R48 and GST-1218 read that bound. Overlaps CEO-3 on the GST-1218 reading.

title: The price-risk paragraph stresses only the session price; the measurement agents, told multiples and VM time that dominate U and X stay fixed
resolution: Add rows to the price-risk paragraph: at a $2.40 agent user U's planned designs cost $2,370 and $2,297 and re-size to 54 x 3 (MDD 19.2); at a $0.80 docs-only pair X's cost $2,184 and $2,204 and re-size to 78 x 3 (MDD 15.6). VM at $0.02 a session sits under R3a's measured VM minutes scaled by the same multiples (about $0.03 for none to $0.14 for autoplan told). Make the agent user's and the docs-only agent's metered price per tree, and VM minutes per arm, explicit admission inputs to the re-size.

title: The futility look needs a random half, a stated conditional power formula on the decision test, and a rule for the shared none arm
resolution: Run tasks in a frozen random order with both arms of a task interleaved, so the half panel is a random half, and define the half as complete task pairs. Compute conditional power on the decision test's z with the B-value formula at the planned drift; at these settings a true effect at the MDD stops about 0.7% of the time and a true zero about 31%, which the prereg should print. Say that when one skill of a family stops, its sibling pays the shared none arm's remaining trials under F1's survivor rule.

title: The ledger can't charge half a shared batch to two skill caps, and no rule says which skill stops when shared spend reaches one cap
resolution: Give each family one ledger item for shared work (crew, slice, authoring, screening, calibration, the none arm on shared tasks) and one item per skill for its own arms. Each skill's ceiling check is its own item plus half the shared item, run as a projection before each part, as R3 amendment 4's between-part check does. Say that a skill's cap stop never stops shared work its sibling needs, and that an unsettled shared lease (src/runner/ledger/ledger.ts:2-4) blocks both skills until it is settled or reconciled; put the reconcile command in the run record.

title: A check that costs under $100 counts only admission's paid calls; the all-in cost to reach the read is $173 to $280 a skill
resolution: State the all-in cost to the admission read per skill and per family in the ELI5, decision 7 and stage 3: half the rig and family build ($125 to $150), half the slice authoring ($8 to $17), calibration ($10 to $29), particle-1's admission ($6 to $23) and the paid admission ($34 to $84) come to about $173 for plan-eng-review, $208 for autoplan, $224 for each X skill and $273 to $280 for each U skill, before the admission prereg's own crew use.

title: Custody isn't sized for bulk panels: TS's sealed bundle was 821 MB for 17 tasks and needed 9 parts
resolution: Keep built task dirs out of sealed bundles: seal statements, hidden tests, checkers and build recipes, and rebuild images from pinned recipes inside the run, as GEVA-173.md:19 suggests. At TS's 48 MB a task, wave 1's roughly 800 valid tasks plus screened-out candidates are on the order of 40 GB of 100 MB parts in the Captain drive. State the sealed size per family, the /dev/shm budget per VM and the leftover check across VMs.

title: Wave 2 and 3 rows assume instruments that wave 1 defers and give them no build line
resolution: Give every wave 2 or 3 row that needs a new instrument a build line at wave 1's rate ($150 to $200 plus a scorer-class /ship): deslop-shared-libs needs the follow-up runner, V10 and blame-linked follow-ups on 108 G tasks (yield unmeasured); learn needs three sequential tasks per repository; context-save and context-restore need a cut-and-resume harness; qa-only needs a report-to-fix runner; spec and office-hours need the oracle user. Mark deslop's 108 x 4 as conditional on a follow-up yield probe. Overlaps CEO-14 on panel reuse.

title: Section 7's table puts design-consultation and design-html at 48 x 3 (20.4); section 8 sizes them at 42 x 4 (19.8)
resolution: Move the Used by entry to a 42 x 4 row at 19.8, or change section 8 to 48 x 3.

title: Target dates leave six days from G admission to the first confirmatory prereg for mining, authoring, sealing and screening about 360 valid G tasks
resolution: Date the G prereg from the T-G slice's measured valid tasks per day and sessions per VM-hour; TS produced 7 valid tasks in one thread, and G's screen alone is 817 Opus sessions.

title: MDDs resolve to 0.6 points and the sizing search picks sizes at grid-step edges
resolution: In the prereg's re-simulation, bisect each MDD to 0.1 points with at least 5,000 simulations a point, as the lane's power.ts requires, and print the Monte Carlo error; a one-step difference such as 14.4 against 15.0 is not a real difference between skills. Reuse power.ts or src/runner/stats/sizing.ts instead of a third model.

title: The stand-in's 1.25 price is never metered before the confirmatory run
resolution: Add 24 stand-in sessions to plan-eng-review's admission (about $16), or price the stand-in at 1.6 times none until it is metered: it runs told's three turns, and E0's plain plan review alone cost $0.236. At 1.6, plan-eng-review's line rises $72 to $1,754.

title: The attached sizing scripts don't run as attached: cost.py and wave23.py read an empty work path, and mddgrid.py execs power.py from another
resolution: Commit the sizing scripts with the prereg (or the plan PR) using relative paths, with a keyless test that reproduces section 7's table and section 8's per-skill lines, so the published numbers can be re-run as AGENTS.md's publish-what-ran rule expects.
